To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) GNNs are not suitable for graph extrapolations, (2) extrapolations can be performed with homomorphism densities, (3) extrapolations can fail if homomorphism densities are not generalized, (4) our counterfactual model is the first of its kind in this field
1) extrapolation on graph sizes is possible, and 2) GNNs fail at extrapolation, while induced homomorphism features succeed, and can be further improved by a GNN substructure decomposition.

1) standard GNNs are incapable of learning graph extrapolation, but 2) GNNs can learn graph extrapolations if the extrapolation task is reduced to a homomorphism density extrapolation, 3) GNNs are capable of learning extrapolations from a single environment, and 4) the extrapolations learned by the GNNs can be used for interpolation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: - How do GNNs extrapolate on different graph sizes? - How do GNSs generalize on different graph classes? - How do we generalize on graph classes with different attributes?
the following questions: (1) How do we extrapolate from a single training dataset? (2) Can graph neural networks extrapolate?
the following question: Can a GNN be trained to extrapolate from a single environment?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
extrapolation is possible in the sense that there are models that can do it, but it is not possible for GNNs, and it is not possible in general, as the number of graphs is infinite.
extrapolation from one graph size to another is not always possible.
extrapolation in graph classification and regression is possible but challenging, and that the current literature has only scratched the surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
extrapolation from one training environment to a different environment is possible for graph classification/regression, but it is a difficult task that requires specialized models.
extrapolating on graph classification/regression can be possible, but it is a hard task and requires careful consideration.
extrapolations in graph regression/classification can be achieved by using a GNN-based subgraph decomposition to induce the homomorphism densities of the target graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that
extrapolation from single training environments can be achieved with the right model.
extrapolation from one training environment to another can be done in a principled way, but it is more difficult than interpolation.
, in certain cases, extrapolating from a single training graph size is possible, and the key is to find a suitable subgraph decomposition that captures the relevant graph features.
